requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL support the specification of record of types and set of types, whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type IS a record whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A set of type IS a set whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type and a set of type ARE denoted using the keyword `of`.
requirements.original: These are denoted using the keyword of.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: An element of a record of type or set of type IS NOT associated with an element identifier.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type IS similar to an ordered array.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A set of type IS similar to an unordered collection.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value, the elements to be changed ARE identified explicitly.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record of-s and set `of-s, elements wished to be changed are identified` explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: In an assignment notation for a record of or set of value, either a value or the not used symbol "-" MAY be assigned to an explicitly identified element.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record of-s and set `of-s, elements wished to be changed are identified` explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value, an element not referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: Other elements, not referred to in the notation, shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: a partial value is specified using the assignment notation
requirements.canonical: When a partial record of or set of value is specified using the assignment notation, only the elements to be assigned values SHALL be specified.
requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, for example, at initialization, only the elements to be assigned values shall be specified: elements not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: 'fields' is used for record of/set of values, which have elements, not fields.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: When a partial record of or set of value is specified using the assignment notation, an element not mentioned IS implicitly left uninitialized.
requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, for example, at initialization, only the elements to be assigned values shall be specified: elements not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: An element of a record of or set of value MAY be left explicitly unspecified in an assignment notation using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: It is also possible to leave fields explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-".

ambiguity.issue: 'fields' is used for record of/set of values, which have elements, not fields.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: a previously initialized value is re-assigned
requirements.canonical: When a previously initialized record of or set of value is re-assigned with an assignment notation, an element that is skipped or assigned the not used symbol "-" SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field or element in an assignment notation, will cause that field or element to remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, every element position up to the last list member SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: When using the value list notation, all elements in the structure shall be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".

ambiguity.issue: 'all elements in the structure' is unclear for record of/set of, whose length is determined by the list; s017 states that trailing elements without list member become uninitialized, so reading 1 was chosen.
readings: In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, every element position up to the last list member SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".
In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, all existing elements of the value SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In a value list notation, the n-th list member IS assigned to the n-th element of the record of or set of value.
requirements.original: The first member of the list is assigned to the first element, the second list member is assigned to the second element, etc. No empty assignment is allowed (e.g. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: A value list notation SHALL NOT contain an empty assignment (two commas with nothing or only white space between them).
requirements.original: The first member of the list is assigned to the first element, the second list member is assigned to the second element, etc. No empty assignment is allowed (e.g. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: An element to be left out of a value list notation assignment SHALL be explicitly skipped in the list by the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: Elements to be left out of the assignment shall be explicitly skipped in the list by use of the not-used-symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: An already initialized element of a record of or set of value that has no corresponding list member at the end of a value list notation IS made uninitialized by the assignment.
requirements.original: Already initialized elements left without a corresponding list member in a value list notation (i.e. at the end of a list) are becoming uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: 'becoming uninitialized' can mean the element stays present with an undefined value, or the element is removed so the length shrinks; example 3 ({0,1,2,3,4} := {0,1,-,2} gives a 4-element value) supports removal, but the text says 'uninitialized'. The text wording was kept.
readings: A trailing initialized element without a corresponding list member IS kept as an uninitialized element and the length of the value IS unchanged.
A trailing initialized element without a corresponding list member IS removed and the length of the value IS reduced to the number of list members.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-value-list
requirements.canonical: Assigning the empty value list notation "{}" to a record of or set of value with initialized elements makes the value empty.
requirements.original: In this way, a value with initialized elements can be made empty by using the empty value list notation ("{}").

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An index notation on the right hand side of an assignment refers to the value of the identified element of a record of or set of value.
requirements.original: The index notation, when used on the right-hand side, refers to the value of the identified element of a record of or a set of.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the index notation is used on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When the index notation is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the value of the identified single element SHALL be changed and the values of the other elements SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When it is used at the left-hand side, only the value of the identified single element is changed, values assigned to other elements already remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index of the first element of a record of or set of value SHALL be zero.
requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero and the index value shall not exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index value in an index notation SHALL NOT exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping of the record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero and the index value shall not exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall not exceed the limitation' does not say whether the index is compared with the upper length bound or with the upper bound minus one (indices start at zero). Reading 1 (index < upper bound) was chosen as consistent with zero-based indexing.
readings: The index value SHALL be less than the upper length bound of the record of or set of type.
The index value SHALL be less than or equal to the upper length bound of the record of or set of type.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: If the element indicated by an index notation on the right hand side of an assignment is uninitialized, this SHALL cause a semantic or runtime error.
requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined (uninitialized), this shall cause a semantic or runtime error.

ambiguity.issue: 'right-hand of an assignment' is used instead of the glossary term 'right hand side (of assignment)'.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element of an uninitialized or omitted record of or set of field or value on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Referencing an identified element of an uninitialized or omitted record of or set of field or value on the right-hand side of an assignment shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the index refers to a non-existent element
requirements.canonical: If an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right hand side IS assigned to that element.
requirements.original: If an indexing operator at the left-hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right-hand side is assigned to the element and all elements with an index smaller than the actual index and without assigned value are created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: the index refers to a non-existent element
requirements.canonical: If an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, every element with a smaller index and without an assigned value IS created with an uninitialized value.
requirements.original: If an indexing operator at the left-hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right-hand side is assigned to the element and all elements with an index smaller than the actual index and without assigned value are created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the record of or set of type is nested
requirements.canonical: For nested record of or set of types, an array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used as a short-hand notation for a nested index notation.
requirements.original: For nested record of or set of types, an array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used as a short-hand notation for a nested index notation.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.condition: the referenced element belongs to an uninitialized or omitted record of/set of value or field
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized record of or set of value or field or of an omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized record of or set of value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When expanding a record of or set of value or value field, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record of or set of type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present and all elements with a smaller index shall be created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When expanding a record of or set of value or value field, all elements with a smaller index than the referenced element SHALL be created with an uninitialized value.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record of or set of type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present and all elements with a smaller index shall be created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: Expansion of record, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:uninitialized-element
requirements.canonical: A record of or set of value SHALL NOT contain uninitialized elements except in transient states while the value remains invisible.
requirements.original: Uninitialized elements are permitted only in transient states (while the value remains invisible).

ambiguity.issue: 'transient states' and 'invisible' are not defined; it is unclear which uses of the value make it visible. Reading 1 was chosen because s032 names sending as the error case.
readings: Uninitialized elements cause an error only when the value becomes externally visible, e.g. when it is sent.
Any use of a record of or set of value containing uninitialized elements other than assignment to its elements (e.g. comparison, passing as a parameter) causes an error.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: Sending a record of or set of value with uninitialized elements SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Sending a record `of` or set of value with uninitialized elements shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: An assignment notation and an index notation used to change elements of a record of or set of value have a similar effect.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When using on the right-hand side of an assignment for record of-s or set `of-s, the assignment` notation and the indexed notation have similar effect, with the exception that the assignment notation is able to address multiple elements in one notation, while the index notation is able to address a single element only.

ambiguity.issue: The note says both notations are used 'on the right-hand side of an assignment', but example 3 shows the equivalent index notation on the left hand side (v_ix[3] := ...). Reading 1 was chosen per example 3.
readings: An assignment notation on the right hand side and an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment have a similar effect.
An assignment notation and an index notation both used on the right hand side of an assignment have a similar effect.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: An assignment notation CAN address multiple elements in one notation, while an index notation CAN address a single element only.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When using on the right-hand side of an assignment for record of-s or set `of-s, the assignment` notation and the indexed notation have similar effect, with the exception that the assignment notation is able to address multiple elements in one notation, while the index notation is able to address a single element only.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation CAN be used to copy record of values element by element in a for loop.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The index notation makes it possible e.g. to copy record of values element by element in a for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: Embedded record of and set of types result in a data structure similar to multidimensional arrays.
requirements.original: Embedded record of and set of types will result in a data structure similar to multidimensional arrays (see clause 15.8.2).

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: The element type of a record of or set of type definition MAY be specified by a nested type definition.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of the aggregated type nested with the record `of or set` `of definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'aggregated type' is used instead of 'structured type'.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define a new record, set, enumerated, set of or record of type.
requirements.original: Both the` definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of and record` `of) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

ambiguity.issue: The parenthesised list omits union types; it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive. Reading 1 (the list is exhaustive as written) was chosen.
readings: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define only a record, set, enumerated, set of or record of type.
A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define any structured type (including union), the list being illustrative.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype-constraint
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY specify subtype constraints.
requirements.original: Both the` definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of and record` `of) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: The inner type of a record of or set of type MAY be referenced by using the index notation with a dash.
requirements.original: It is also allowed to reference the inner type of record of and set of types by using the index notation but with a dash.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: The notation TypeId[-], where TypeId resolves to the name of a record of or set of type, references the inner type of TypeId.
requirements.original: The notation TypeId[-], where TypeId resolves to the name of a record of or set of type, references the inner type of TypeId.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.condition: the type definition restricts the element type
requirements.canonical: If the type definition of a record of or set of type restricts its element type, the inner type reference yields a type which contains all values of the constrained element type.
requirements.original: If the type definition restricts the element type of the record of or set of type, referencing the inner type of that type yields a type which contains all values from the constrained type.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains all values from the constrained type' does not state whether the yielded type is exactly the constrained element type or may be wider. Example (ConstrainedRecordOfInt[-]) shows the element constraint is kept, so reading 1 was chosen.
readings: The inner type reference yields exactly the constrained element type (the element subtype constraint is kept).
The inner type reference yields a type that includes all values of the constrained element type, possibly the unconstrained element type.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of the outer record of type IS NOT part of the inner type yielded by an inner type reference.

non_requirement.reason: pointer to clause 6.2.13 for subtyping of record of and set of types
introduces the example function in 6.2.3.0-s038 illustrating NOTE 3
